description:
FOUND s504c (#2633, member 4 of the brief).  After #2633 a promoted file lexical in a non-program unit (eval STRING, do FILE, require/use) is a unit-unique cell $x__file__N, but for a SCALAR in a unit that contains a string eval the M-F alias (ir-spec 9.1) still writes that cell into the ORIGINAL-name global of the declaring package.  So half of #2633's collision (I) survives for exactly those units:
  w7-shape + eval: main `$c = "gc"; do "./q07d.pl"; print "main: $c"`, q07d.pl `my $c = sub { "C" }; sub t7 { eval q{sub { package Other; $c->() }} } print t7()->(); 1;`  perl `main: gc`, PCL `main: CODE(0x1)`.
  Also: /home/bernt/pcl/.claude/worktrees/agent-a41c97e5832f266e1/scratch/s504c/probes/q13.pl (regexp.t head + `eval q{print "$file"}`: perl main: outer, PCL main: inner), q05.pl ($s), r4.pl (module ModE: user's `$ModE::bb = "u"` lands in the module's lexical).  Reproducers in /home/bernt/pcl/.claude/worktrees/agent-a41c97e5832f266e1/scratch/s504c/probes/ (and /home/bernt/pcl-agent-scratch/s504/review/w7.pl, v2.pl).

MEASURED (s504c): a tree with the alias suppressed for non-program units (scratch extraction, never committed) fixes q07, q13 and keeps q06 (a nested eval inside an eval-defined sub) working, BUT the full perl-tests sweep loses 8 rows: eval.t 56-63 = perl's t/op/eval.t lines 289-311, `eval q{ my $yyy = 9; sub fred3 { ... eval '$yyy' ... } ... }` -- a NAMED sub defined inside an eval string whose own runtime eval names the eval-unit's file lexical: the #2285 publication reaches the outer eval's sites, not the sub-body eval's, so the global fall-through (the alias) is the only path.  Everything else in the sweep was identical (TOTAL 18706 vs 18714, the 8 rows only).

NEXT (design): give the sub-body eval sites of a non-program unit the unit's published pairs (the capture alist), so the alias can be dropped for non-program units; bar = eval.t 56-63 stay, q07/q13/r4 == perl.
subject: The #2633 ALIAS residue: in a non-program unit with a string eval, a mangled SCALAR cell still gets (p-alias-eval-cell '$x cell) at its decl, which REPLACES the caller`s same-named package global while the alias stands (do-file `my $c=sub{...}; sub t { eval q{...$c...} }` leaves the caller`s $main::c = CODE) -- measured: the alias is still NEEDED for eval.t 56-63
